messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: renderUI
parts:
The reason that the save isn't called is because of a recent change so that non-visible objects in `output` are now suspended. 

Here's the code in question:

output$save <- reactive({
    cat("Save called\n")
    save = input$save;
    if(is.null(save) || save ==0)
      return(NULL)
    isolate({
      cat("Saved\n")
      updatePatient()  
      updateRecord()
    })
})

The recent change makes it so that output objects are suspended when they're not visible -- in other words, they will only execute when they're visible in the web browser. Since 'output$save' isn't used by the UI at all (the actionButton named 'save' is separate), it will always be suspended, and therefore will never execute.

The way to use reactive expressions that aren't connect to the 'output' object is to use observe(), like this:

observe({
    cat("Save called\n")
    save = input$save;
    if(is.null(save) || save ==0)
      return(NULL)
    isolate({
      cat("Saved\n")
      updatePatient()  
      updateRecord()
    })
})

There's no need to store the result as output$save.

Although it isn't well documented, this actually has always been the correct way to do it... We're working on some documentation for the tutorial explaining reactivity, and it will cover this topic.


Regarding the deprecation messages, you're right that it wasn't working -- there was a commit that wasn't properly added to the main branch and pushed to github. It should be there now.

-Winston
